page.layout: One column of running text, with a running head above it. No marginal notes, page number or signature. Catchword "nam" at the lower right.

main_text.p: Arabum, tam scribendi, quàm pronunciandi in plerisque, mori adhæsisse, non satis ea, quo vulgo efferri vel appellari solent, modo ex-pressisse ratos, cùm nihil in Arabum libris, vel transcribendis vel transferendis, plurium er-rorum (imo monstrorum) causa fuerit, quam hac ex parte incuria. nec tamen, cum nimis frequenter puncta literarum [illegible, ~6 letters] diacritica omittere, vel mutare soleant Scribæ, in om-nibus, quod volui affectum me polliceri aufim.Si cui exemplaria magis fida conti-gerint, sicubi erratum sit, facile erit corrigere. In exprimendo autem Latinis literis Arabi-ca, si à more recepto alicubi recefferim, fa-ctum hoc in nostratium gratiam, qui certé A-rabicis pronunciandis apti satis nati sunt, nec tamen omnes Alphabeti Latini literas, eo, quo alii modo efferunt. Hanc ob causam cum Arabum ǧ vulgo, nec ineptè per Italo- rum gi exprimatur, & g Anglico, suo loco re-spondeat, quia tamen non est ea constans apud nos istius literæ sonus, adeo ut viris non indoctis erroris hæc aliquando causa fuerit, malui istam ipsorum literam per j confo-nam

page.notes: The Greek word after "literarum" (a note on iota, with a second word) is too small to read with certainty, so it is marked illegible. The Arabic-transliteration letter after "Arabum" (g with a diacritic) is doubtful; it is copied as ǧ. The space after "aufim." is missing in the print and is left as printed. The first word "Arabum" is a fragment carried over from the previous page. The catchword "nam" is printed at the lower right.
